messages.text: Brundle: Debating the rule that cost Norris and why Madring needs changes

metadata.summary: The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers.
metadata.content: Martin Brundle's verdict on Madring's F1 debut, the areas to change for 2027 and Virtual Safety Car rules | F1 News | Sky Sports Skip to content Opinion Martin Brundle's verdict on Madring's F1 debut, the areas to change for 2027 and Virtual Safety Car rules Sky Sports F1's Martin Brundle delves into the talking points from the Spanish Grand Prix, assessing F1's newest venue and where it can be improved, the debate around the rules that cost Lando Norris, and Kimi Antonelli's ever-growing world championship lead Martin Brundle Expert Analyst @MBrundleF1 Monday 14 September 2026 16:23, UK Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player See how Lando Norris lost the lead and a likely win at the Spanish Grand Prix after an untimely Virtual Safety Car for the McLaren driver The inaugural Madring grand prix was ok, the new venue offering some interesting aspects such as the long and banked turn 12 and testing high-speed sections between continuous and unrelenting walls and barriers. It all had a feeling of work in progress. We know they lost a lot of time in the build process with particularly bad weather, and as a temporary race track adjacent to the international airport, and effectively racing around the Madrid equivalent of the Birmingham NEC, it had its challenges. The pitlane and paddock were simply vast, creating some logistical challenges for all and, much more importantly, the track layout was not conducive to overtaking, to say the least. messages.text: Carra: Arteta becoming like Sir Alex after ref criticism

metadata.summary: Jamie Carragher says Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta is "becoming the Sir Alex Ferguson of the Premier League" after strongly criticising the penalty awarded against his side in Saturday's 2-0 win at Sunderland.

A furious Arteta described the saved second-half penalty as "unacceptable" after referee John Brooks pointed to the spot when Arsenal defender Ezri Konsa brought down Dan Ballard. The Gunners have subsequently sought an explanation from refereeing body Pro Ref over the penalty award.
